question: What is the primary purpose of performing a surgical tracheotomy?
explanation: A tracheotomy creates an alternative airway path when the upper respiratory tract is blocked or compromised. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is a tracheostomy preferred over long-term endotracheal intubation?

options.A: It completely eliminates the risk of bacterial infection
options.B: It allows the patient to speak normally immediately
options.C: It requires zero daily cleaning or specialized maintenance
options.D: It prevents long-term damage to the vocal cords

explanation: Prolonged oral tubes press against delicate laryngeal structures, whereas a tracheal opening avoids the vocal cords entirely. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h1)

question: Between which tracheal rings is a standard surgical tracheostomy typically created?
explanation: Surgeons target the upper tracheal rings to ensure a secure stoma placement while avoiding deep mediastinal structures. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h2)

question: A major anatomical risk during a tracheotomy procedure involves accidental damage to which nearby structure?
explanation: The thyroid gland overlies the upper tracheal rings and requires careful retraction or surgical division during the procedure. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the obturator during a tracheostomy insertion?

options.A: Securing the mechanical ventilator tubing tightly
options.B: Collecting thick pulmonary secretions inside the lumen
options.C: Preventing accidental decannulation by the patient
options.D: Guiding safe tube insertion without mucosal trauma

explanation: The obturator features a smooth, rounded tip that shields the tracheal tissue from the sharp edge of the outer cannula during placement. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why must a nurse inspect the inner cannula during routine shift assessments?

options.A: To measure the exact depth of the tracheal rings
options.B: To deflate the cuff before speaking trials begin
options.C: To check if the patient requires an increase in oxygen flow
options.D: To prevent dangerous blockages from accumulated dried secretions

explanation: Inner cannulas collect mucus and must be cleaned or replaced periodically to maintain a clear airway lumen. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h3)

question: How tight should the tracheostomy securing ties be adjusted around the patient's neck?

options.A: Secured only with metal clips instead of cloth
options.B: Loose enough to slide three fingers easily sideways
options.C: Allowing one finger to fit comfortably underneath
options.D: Tied as tightly as possible to stop any movement

explanation: This tension ensures the tube stays anchored while preventing pressure ulcers on the delicate neck skin. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is a two-person technique recommended when changing ties on a fresh tracheostomy tube?

options.A: To ensure accurate measurement of blood oxygen levels
options.B: To speed up the sterile dressing application process
options.C: To prevent accidental decannulation before the tract matures
options.D: To assist the patient with deep breathing exercises

explanation: A fresh stoma lacks a stable tract, meaning a single cough can dislodge the tube if it is unanchored. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended duration for a single pass of tracheal suctioning?
explanation: Prolonged suctioning removes vital oxygen from the airway, leading to severe hypoxemia and cardiac rhythm changes. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h5)

question: When should a nurse initiate tracheal suctioning for a patient with a tracheostomy?

options.A: Immediately after every meal regardless of lung sounds
options.B: Strictly every two hours around the clock without exception
options.C: Only when the patient requests it verbally
options.D: When coarse breath sounds and visible secretions are present

explanation: Suctioning is done based on clinical need to avoid unnecessary trauma to the delicate tracheal mucosa. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h5)

question: What equipment must always be kept immediately available at the bedside of any tracheostomy patient?

options.A: An oral endotracheal intubation kit with a laryngoscope
options.B: A mechanical ventilator backup power generator
options.C: A spare tracheostomy tube of equal and smaller size
options.D: A sterile surgical scalpel and deep retractor set

explanation: Immediate bedside availability of replacement tubes ensures rapid management if accidental decannulation occurs. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe immediate action when a fresh tracheostomy tube accidentally dislodges?

options.A: Calling for immediate medical or emergency assistance
options.B: Applying bag-valve ventilation over the stoma if needed
options.C: Forcing a larger tube into the immature tract forcefully
options.D: Using the obturator to guide a replacement tube gently

explanation: Forcing an oversized or misaligned tube causes severe tissue trauma and false passage formation. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h6)

question: What indicates that a tracheostomy patient is ready for permanent decannulation?

options.A: Tolerating complete tube capping without distress
options.B: Completing ten days of continuous humidification
options.C: Demonstrating the ability to swallow liquid foods
options.D: Having normal blood pressure for three days

explanation: Capping tests whether the patient can breathe comfortably through their upper airway before the stoma is closed. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h7)

question: How does the stoma typically close after a successful tracheostomy decannulation?

options.A: It requires immediate surgical suturing in the operating room
options.B: It closes instantly once a pressure bandage is applied
options.C: It heals naturally by secondary intention with a simple dressing
options.D: It stays permanently open unless grafted with synthetic skin

explanation: Most stomas close on their own within a few days once the tube is removed and covered with a sterile occlusive dressing. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h7)
